description: Minimal capability set for the Control Panel window (NFR-14). Permissions are added by the item whose FR actually needs them, never in anticipation. Granted today, and nothing else: core:event:default (allow-listen, allow-unlisten, allow-emit, allow-emit-to) — the frontend<->backend event bus, and the slide-advance hot path, which broadcasts an event instead of awaiting a command (PRD 6.5); and allow-list-monitors, the app-defined permission defined in src-tauri/permissions/list_monitors.json, which is what makes commands::display::list_monitors callable at all. THAT SECOND ENTRY CHANGED THE MEANING OF THIS FILE (SEC-01, ADR-0041). Since src-tauri/permissions/ exists this application ships an ACL manifest, so app-defined commands are gated exactly like plugin: ones and "windows": ["main"] below finally binds them too — it bound plugin: commands only for as long as there was no manifest. The consequence is fail-closed, and reopening it takes a rebuild: every app-defined command in generate_handler! must be named by some capability or it is rejected at invoke time with 'Command {} not allowed by ACL'. dynamic-acl is off (ADR-0013), which removes Manager::add_capability and nothing else — Context::runtime_authority_mut and RuntimeAuthority::__allow_command are pub and not behind that feature, and the latter grants windows:["*"], so 'no runtime escape' would be too strong; what is true is that reaching either takes Rust code in this crate, hence a diff, which scripts/check-command-inventory.js rejects by name — a grep over src-tauri/src/, so it catches what lands in this crate and not an alias, a macro, a re-export or another crate. Note also that this gate does not cover plugin:__TAURI_CHANNEL__|fetch, which tauri exempts inside the condition itself (webview/mod.rs:1823-1826); see src-tauri/src/commands/mod.rs. src-tauri/commands.inventory.md is the list to work from, and scripts/check-command-inventory.js is red until the definitions, the registrations, the inventory and the capability grants all name the same set. Deliberately NOT granted: core:default, which also pulls in core:app, core:path, core:image, core:resources, core:menu, core:tray and core:webview; and core:window:default, whose 28 permissions include allow-available-monitors, allow-primary-monitor, allow-current-monitor and allow-monitor-from-point. Display enumeration is a backend responsibility (FR-101) and the output window's whole lifecycle belongs to the Rust Display Service (PRD 6.3); granting the window API would open a second, ACL-legitimate path to the same facts and leave the frontend with two sources of truth. The main window is created from tauri.conf.json, not from the frontend, so no window permission is needed at all. No filesystem, dialog, shell or HTTP permission is granted either. And the window list is a literal, never a glob: the output window is granted zero app-defined commands, which capabilities/output-window.json exists to say out loud, and a "*" here would hand them all back to it in one character.
